title: US stocks today: Nasdaq rebounds as chip stocks recover from steep losses, rate fears persist
summary: US stocks rebound as chipmakers recover from Thursday's steep AI-led selloff, lifting the Nasdaq 1.73%. Nvidia, AMD, Intel and Micron lead the recovery, while stronger-than-expected October jobs data revive concerns over a December Fed rate hike. Airbnb rallies after raising its full-year revenue growth forecast, while Atlassian shares decline.

title: Sugar output jumps to nearly 13 lakh tonnes so far in 2026-27 market year: ISMA
summary: Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA), in a statement on Friday, said the 184 sugar mills have commenced crushing operations across the country as of November 5, 2026, compared to 154 mills during the corresponding period of the preceding year.

title: Arini’s Hedge Fund Losses Grow to 32% as It Sells Some Positions
summary: Losses at Arini Capital Management’s main hedge fund deepened in the final days of October, taking declines to 32% for the year, according to a letter to investors seen by Bloomberg.

title: Elanco Shares Jump After Q3 Beat and Outlook Raise
summary: Elanco Animal Health shares rose nearly 8% after the company reported third-quarter earnings above expectations and raised its full-year outlook. Jeff Simmons, Elanco’s President and CEO, called it a high-quality quarter, citing 11% reported growth and broad strength across markets and product lines. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

States' capital outlay to accelerate to 10-12% on Centre support in FY27, urban infra to lead: Crisil
summary: States' capital expenditure is projected to rise 10-12% to around Rs 8.5 lakh crore in FY27, driven by higher central assistance and greater fiscal flexibility, according to a Crisil Ratings report. Increased allocation under the SASCI scheme is expected to support infrastructure spending, particularly urban development, roads and bridges.

title: FIGS Beats Earnings as Demand Outstrips Supply, CEO Trina Spear Says
